newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Xinjiang basins' crude oil output seen up.
newsitem.headline: China's Xinjiang basins' crude oil output seen up.

text.p: The Tarim, Junggar and Turpan-Hami basins in China's western region of Xinjiang will have combined crude oil production capacity of 17 million tonnes by the end of 1997, the Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
That compared with the current 15 million tonnes, Xinhua said, quoting an official of the China National Petroleum Corp.
The three basins would have 1.5 billion tonnes in proven oil reserves and crude output of 24 million tonnes by the year 2000, the official said.

Xinjiang had entered a peak period of oil and gas exploration, Xinhua said, adding that 40 oil and gas fields in the region had been discovered in the three basins with total proven reserves of two billion tonnes of oil.
The Junggar oilfield was expected to put its Xiaoguai field, which had proven reserves of 59 million tonnes, into operation this year, the agency said.
